Cc: Lisa Chen <l.chen@novacorp.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request to split SOW + request for repricing (NovaCorp)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement reviewed the draft MSA and the current Order Form and we have two items that need to be reflected as a formal change order before legal will sign:

1) Split the SOW: NovaCorp wants the integration services SOW separated from the production capacity Order Form so we can route the SOW through professional services budget.
2) Repricing for Year 2: Updated usage forecast (attached) increases committed throughput by ~45% in year 2 — we need an updated fee schedule and a clear approach to amortizing onboarding credits.

Attached: redline_MSA_v3.docx (initial redlines), SOW_v2_marked.pdf (requested split).

Can you confirm next steps and an estimated turn-around for Redwood legal? We’d like to get these changes captured in a single change order to avoid multiple DocuSign flows.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Senior Procurement Manager
NovaCorp

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@novacorp.com>, Lisa Chen <l.chen@novacorp.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request to split SOW + request for repricing (NovaCorp)

Jordan / Maya —

Reviewed the SOW markups. A few technical notes that should be reflected in the split SOW and Order Form:

- Implementation SOW (new doc): include milestone-based acceptance for the integration phase (3 deliverables, 30/40/30 percent). We should avoid tying production credits to milestone acceptance — keep financials in the Order Form.
- Capacity Order Form: the forecasted +45% in year 2 increases sustained GPU hours; we can offer a committed throughput discount rather than change per-token pricing.
- Cache/eviction SLA: current MSA references cache behavior — NovaCorp should accept the standard caching practice we documented; if they need a guaranteed KV persistence, that’s a premium.

I attached a quick pricing_model.csv with two scenarios: (A) keep per-token rate, add committed throughput discount; (B) reduce per-token rate but add a minimum monthly commitment. My recommendation: Scenario A — simpler for NovaCorp’s procurement.

I can draft the technical Annex for the split SOW and mark the acceptance criteria. Will coordinate with Laura on any cross-references to the MSA.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

[attachment] pricing_model.csv (text/csv)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@novacorp.com>, Lisa Chen <l.chen@novacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request to split SOW + request for repricing (NovaCorp)

Jordan / team / NovaCorp —

I reviewed the redline_MSA_v3.docx and prepared a counter-redline focused on three areas:

1) Termination for convenience: NovaCorp’s change adds a 30-day termination for convenience with pro-rated credits. We can accept a 90-day notice or 30-day with a defined wind-down payment (to protect reserved capacity).
2) Data residency & audit logs: they requested expanding audit rights to include on-demand audits. We can offer quarterly audit windows and SOC 2 evidence; on-demand audits are accepted but limited to once per 12 months and with a scoped set of logs.
3) Liability cap and indemnities: tightened language in their redline — we retained our standard liability cap but added a carve for breach of confidentiality and security incidents.

I’ve uploaded combined_redline_20270524.docx which contains tracked changes and inline comments where we need clarification (e.g., whether NovaCorp’s counsel expects the SOW split to change the governing law clause — we typically keep governing law at the MSA level).

Please review: notable comments are on pages 2, 5, and the new Exhibit A (implementation milestones).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

[attachment] combined_redline_20270524.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Quick finance note —

If we accept Scenario A (committed throughput discount), the effective ARR impact is neutral in Y1 but reduces ASR in Y2 by ~12% versus NovaCorp’s asked rate card. To approve the discount we need:
- Sales approval (Jordan) — confirms strategic value of NovaCorp expansion.
- Finance sign-off for deferred onboarding credit amortization (I propose 12-month amortization).

Also, any wind-down payment proposed by Legal should be modeled into the revenue recognition schedule. I’ll produce a short P&L delta and circulate by EOD.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference
